metadata.title: Hosea
metadata.subtitle: Hosea 1:1 – 14:9 (43 questions)
metadata.description: Questions on the Book of Hosea according to the King James Version (1769).
metadata.author: King James Version (1769)

questions.text: What command did the LORD give unto Hosea at the beginning (Hosea 1:2)?

options.text: To offer a sacrifice in the holy temple at Jerusalem for the sins of people
Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms, for the land hath departed from God
To build an altar on Mount Carmel and call upon the prophets of strange gods
To proclaim war against the king of Assyria and muster all the tribes of land

questions.text: What does the name Lo-ruhamah signify in Hosea 1:6?

options.text: I will be your God and show great mercy unto you for ever
I will bless you abundantly and never chastise your house
I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel
I will bring you up out of Egypt and make you a great nation

questions.text: What name was given to Hosea's third child and what does it mean (Hosea 1:8-9)?

options.text: Immanuel: God with us, for the LORD will never leave His children
Lo-ruhamah: I will no more have mercy upon the rebellious people
Jezreel: God soweth, for the LORD will scatter His chosen seed
Lo-ammi: Call his name Lo-ammi, for ye are not my people

questions.text: What promise follows the word Lo-ammi in Hosea 1:10?

options.text: Where it was said: Ye are not my people, there it shall be said: Sons of God
The children of Israel shall be scattered among all nations and humiliated
The princes of Israel shall serve the king of Asshur and pay yearly tribute
The people shall pay the sacred tithe and be blessed in the fertile land

questions.text: What ignorance of Israel is rebuked in Hosea 2:8?

options.text: She thought the king had given her corn, and wine, and oil
She did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil
She thought her harvest came by her own labour and wisdom
She thought her fathers had left her corn, and wine, and oil

questions.text: How will the LORD win back His unfaithful bride in Hosea 2:14?

options.text: He will buy her with gifts and give her gold and silver
He will compel her by judgment and drive her into the wilderness
He will allure her, bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her
He will call her by a messenger and proclaim mercy unto her

questions.text: What shall Israel call the LORD in that day according to Hosea 2:16?

options.text: Thou shalt call me my Lord, and no more my God
Thou shalt call me my Shepherd, and no more my Judge
Thou shalt call me my Father, and no more my King
Thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali

questions.text: For what price did Hosea buy back his wife in Hosea 3:2?

options.text: For fifteen pieces of silver, and an homer and half homer of barley
For thirty pieces of silver, and two full homers of choice wheat
For fifty pieces of silver, and three full homers of pure spelt
For ten pieces of silver, and an half homer of unthreshed wheat

questions.text: What condition is foretold for the children of Israel in Hosea 3:4?

options.text: They shall dwell in peace under a new king and offer sacrifices continually
Israel shall abide many days without king, prince, sacrifice, image, ephod
They shall offer sacrifices in abundance and adorn the temple with gold
They shall find a new home in Babylon and serve there without a king

questions.text: Whom shall the children of Israel seek in the latter days (Hosea 3:5)?

options.text: The gods of the neighbouring nations and their kings
The high priest and the elders of the people
The LORD their God, and David their king
The prince of Assyria and his protector

questions.text: What does the LORD find lacking in the land according to Hosea 4:1?

options.text: Obedience, order, and diligence
Righteousness, wisdom, and peace
Sacrifice, prayer, and fasting
Truth, mercy, and knowledge of God

questions.text: Why are the priests rejected by the LORD in Hosea 4:6?

options.text: Because thou hast rejected knowledge and forgotten the law of thy God
Because they offer too little and neglect the feasts of the LORD
Because they obey not the king and lead the whole people astray
Because they have forsaken the sanctuary and serve strange gods

questions.text: What caused the people to err according to Hosea 4:12?

options.text: Envy of the neighbouring nations and their gods
The spirit of whoredoms, which caused them to err from their God
Pride in the temple and its splendour
Famine in the land and the distress of the poor

questions.text: What happens when they go with flocks and herds to seek the LORD (Hosea 5:6)?

options.text: They are heard, for the LORD hath respect unto their gifts
They find him straightway, for he is nigh
They shall not find him; he hath withdrawn himself from them
They are blessed, for they offer much

questions.text: Unto whom did Ephraim send when he saw his sickness (Hosea 5:13)?

options.text: Unto the prophets in Jerusalem, that they might counsel him
Unto the Egyptians, that they should send him horses
Unto the Syrians, which promised him help
Unto the Assyrian, and sent to king Jareb: yet could he not heal

questions.text: Until when will the LORD return unto His place in Hosea 5:15?

options.text: Till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face
Till they bring him an offering and present their gifts
Till they make peace with Assyria and pay tribute
Till a new king reign and deliver the land

questions.text: What confidence is expressed in the call to repentance in Hosea 6:1-2?

options.text: The LORD hath forsaken us and will never return unto us
He hath torn, and he will heal; in the third day he will raise us up
The LORD forgetteth our sin at once and healeth us immediately
The LORD sendeth us a new king and delivereth us out of distress

questions.text: Unto what is the goodness of Ephraim and Judah likened in Hosea 6:4?

options.text: Unto a tree by the waters that ever beareth fruit
Unto a river that never faileth and ever floweth
Unto a morning cloud, and the early dew that goeth away
Unto a rock in the storm that standeth unmoved

questions.text: What does the LORD desire according to Hosea 6:6?

options.text: Fasting and mourning more than songs of praise
Sacrifices and gifts more than the knowledge of God
Incense and prayer more than mercy
Mercy and the knowledge of God more than sacrifice

questions.text: Unto what is Ephraim, who hath mixed himself among the people, likened in Hosea 7:8?

options.text: Unto a cake not turned
Unto a dove without a nest, that fluttereth to and fro
Unto an oven without fire, that baketh nothing
Unto a pitcher without water, that no man filleth

questions.text: Unto what is Ephraim likened in Hosea 7:11?

options.text: Unto an eagle that soareth high above the mountain tops
Like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, go to Assyria
Unto a roaring lion seeking prey in the forests of Lebanon
Unto a swift deer that fleeth before the huntsmen in fields

questions.text: What image does Hosea 7:4 use for the adulterers?

options.text: A fire upon the mountain, which the baker never quencheth
A fountain that drieth up in summer
An oven heated by the baker
An oven that groweth cold while the baker sleepeth

questions.text: What proverb concerning judgment is declared in Hosea 8:7?

options.text: He that diggeth a pit shall fall headlong into the same
He that soweth righteousness shall reap life everlasting
The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children suffer
For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind

questions.text: What does Hosea 8:5 say concerning the calf of Samaria?

options.text: Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off; mine anger is kindled against them
The LORD blesseth it and heareth the people that pray before it
The LORD suffereth it and overlooketh it for his patience' sake
The LORD useth it as a sign of his presence among the people

questions.text: How did Israel regard the great things of God's law (Hosea 8:12)?

options.text: As the highest good, held in honour and kept exactly in all points
As a strange thing, though the great things of his law were written
As a burden gladly borne and never laid aside, for it maketh life easier
As an old tradition of the fathers, to be faithfully kept and handed down

questions.text: How does the LORD describe his delight in Israel in the wilderness in Hosea 9:10?

options.text: As dew in the morning and as rain in the spring upon the field
As gold in the fire and as silver in the furnace of the refiner
Like grapes in the wilderness, and as the firstripe in the fig tree
As pearls in the sea and as precious stones in the mountains of Israel

questions.text: What curse shall come upon Ephraim according to Hosea 9:11?

options.text: His flocks shall be carried away, and his land become a wilderness where no cattle feed
His harvest shall wither in the field, and his cities be forsaken of their inhabitants
His cities shall be destroyed, and his people scattered among the nations
Their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception

questions.text: Unto what lot does the LORD consign the people in Hosea 9:17?

options.text: They shall be wanderers among the nations
They shall serve in captivity and bow down to strange gods
They shall dwell in the wilderness and seek their bread there
They shall live without king and sacrifice and be put to silence

questions.text: How did Israel's altars multiply according to Hosea 10:1?

options.text: The more fruit it bare, the more sacrifices it gave unto God
According to the multitude of fruit it increased the altars
The less fruit it bare, the more altars of stone it built up
According to the wealth of the land it made fewer altars there

questions.text: What shall they say to the mountains and hills in Hosea 10:8?

options.text: Hide us from the king; and to the hills, Protect us
Shelter us; and to the hills, Hide us
Cover us; and to the hills, Fall on us
Give us water; and to the hills, Carry us

questions.text: What does the LORD command His people to do in Hosea 10:12?

options.text: Keep the fast and the sabbath, then the LORD will come and rain righteousness upon you
Build new altars and offer more and more, then the LORD will surely hear you
Go to war against Assyria and trust steadfastly in the LORD your God
Sow in righteousness, reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground: for it is time to seek the LORD

questions.text: Which verse of Hosea is quoted in the Gospel of Matthew (Hosea 11:1)?

options.text: I called my son out of Egypt
I have called thee by thy name
I will send my messenger
I will pour out my spirit

questions.text: How does Hosea 11:3 describe the loving care of the LORD for Ephraim?

options.text: He chastened him with rods and stripes, but they laid not the correction to heart
He took Ephraim by his arms and led him, but they knew not that he healed them
He left him alone, that he might find his own way and learn thereby
He gave him statutes and commandments, but they kept them not

questions.text: What tender cry breaks from the heart of the LORD in Hosea 11:8?

options.text: I have forsaken thee, Ephraim, and I will not receive thee again
I will destroy thee, Ephraim, as Admah and Zeboim
How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? mine heart is turned within me
I will never look upon thee again, Ephraim, for thou hast forsaken me

questions.text: What event in Jacob's life is recalled in Hosea 12:4?

options.text: He went down into Egypt unto Joseph with all his house
He blessed the sons of Joseph with his hands crossed
He bought the birthright and obtained the blessing
He had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication

questions.text: What admonition is given in Hosea 12:6?

options.text: Turn thou to thy God: keep mercy and judgment, wait on God continually
Flee to the mountains and hide thyself until the judgment of God be overpast
Offer sacrifices in the temple and keep all the feasts of the LORD according to the law of Moses
Make peace with thy neighbours and trust in their help in time of trouble

questions.text: What boast does Ephraim make in Hosea 12:8?

options.text: I am strong, mine host is great, I have no enemy to fear
I am become rich, I have found me out substance; they shall find none iniquity in me
I am wise, my counsel is good, I need no prophet
I am devout, I offer much, I have done no evil

questions.text: What does the LORD testify concerning Himself in Hosea 13:4?

options.text: I am the maker of heaven and earth; there is none else beside me
I am the God of the fathers, who chose and led Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt; there is no saviour beside me
I am the King of Zion, who ruleth over all nations for ever

questions.text: What cry unto death and the grave is proclaimed in Hosea 13:14?

options.text: O death, I fear thee not, for I have long since overcome thee
O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? I have overcome you
O death, thou art swallowed up in victory; O grave, thou art overthrown and destroyed
O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction

questions.text: What effect did Israel's pasture and prosperity have (Hosea 13:6)?

options.text: They were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me
They gave thanks unto the LORD and became generous
They became generous and dealt their bread to the poor
They made a league with Assyria and trusted in his might

questions.text: What should the penitent take with them according to Hosea 14:2?

options.text: Costly burnt offerings of rams, as commanded in the holy law
Take with you words, and turn to LORD: so will we render calves of lips
Silver and gold to enrich the sanctuary and support holy priests
Firstfruits of the vintage to appease the anger of the Almighty

questions.text: What gracious promise does the LORD give in Hosea 14:4?

options.text: I will chastise them in measure until they seek my holy face
I will lead them into Babylon and speak comfortable words there
I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely and turn wrath
I will cause them to wait seven seasons until they cry for aid

questions.text: With what declaration does the Book of Hosea conclude (Hosea 14:9)?

options.text: The LORD cometh to judge all the nations and kingdoms of the earth
The LORD is King for ever, and all nations serve him gladly
The LORD will save Israel and gather all his people again
The ways of the LORD are right, and the just shall walk in them
